claims.text: At stage-3 no file under DonHang.App/lib/screens names a color; screens pass StatusBanner a tone.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-3: git grep -i color -- DonHang.App/lib/screens (no match)

claims.text: Brand (lib/design/brand.dart) has three fields: Color seed, StatusColors lightStatus, StatusColors darkStatus; statusColors(brightness) returns darkStatus for Brightness.dark, else lightStatus.
donHangBrand is the only Brand in lib/; its seed is Colors.indigo, with four StatusColors values (warning, onWarning, success, onSuccess) for light and four for dark.

buildTheme(brand, brightness) returns ThemeData(colorSchemeSeed: brand.seed, brightness: brightness, extensions: [brand.statusColors(brightness)]); it is the only place under lib/ that constructs a ThemeData. extensions is where ThemeData keeps StatusColors.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-3: DonHang.App/lib/design/theme.dart:11-17; git grep 'ThemeData(' -- DonHang.App/lib

claims.text: main.dart passes theme: buildTheme(donHangBrand, Brightness.light) and darkTheme: buildTheme(donHangBrand, Brightness.dark) to MaterialApp.router.
ThemeData's colorSchemeSeed generates the theme's ColorScheme with ColorScheme.fromSeed, using the seed and the given brightness.
claims.source_hint: Flutter API: ThemeData constructor, colorSchemeSeed parameter; ColorScheme.fromSeed

claims.text: StatusBanner reads secondaryContainer from ColorScheme for info and warning from the StatusColors extension; no component receives a Brand.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-3: DonHang.App/lib/design/components/status_banner.dart:30-39; git grep Brand -- DonHang.App/lib/design/components

claims.text: testBrand in brand_theme_test.dart has seed Colors.teal and its own StatusColors for light and dark.

brand_theme_test runs one testWidgets per Brightness.values; under buildTheme(testBrand, brightness) an info StatusBanner's Material color equals ColorScheme.fromSeed(teal, brightness).secondaryContainer and a warning one equals testBrand's warning.
Brightness has two values, light and dark, so iterating Brightness.values runs the test twice.
backgroundOf finds the first Material descendant of StatusBanner and returns its color; a further test checks donHangBrand's and testBrand's light secondaryContainer differ.

no_raw_colors_test lists every .dart file under lib/ recursively except lib/design/brand.dart, normalises '\' to '/', and records path:line: text of each line matching \bColors\.|\bColor\(; it expects the list to be empty.
The Dart RegExp \bColors\.|\bColor\( matches 'Colors.teal' and 'Color(0xFF7A5900)' but not 'Color' without '(' nor 'Color.fromARGB('.
claims.source_hint: Dart API: dart:core RegExp (JavaScript regular expression semantics, \b word boundary)

claims.text: When expect(actual, isEmpty, reason: ...) fails on a non-empty list, the failure message shows the actual list and the reason.
claims.source_hint: package:matcher / flutter_test: expect, reason parameter, isEmpty

claims.text: Directory('lib') is resolved against the working directory; flutter test runs with DonHang.App/ as working directory, and File.path uses '\' on Windows.
claims.source_hint: Dart API: dart:io Directory, FileSystemEntity.path; flutter test docs

claims.text: Supporting a second brand by copying screens doubles every later fix and lets the copies drift; when screens hold no color, a second Brand value is enough.
A raw color compiles and looks right while only one brand ships, so build and manual checks miss it; a test guard is worth having when more than one brand is planned or possible.
In DonHang.App warning and success colors are written by hand in each Brand per brightness; they are not generated from the seed.
At stage-3 `grep -rn -E "Colors\.|Color\(" DonHang.App/lib` prints 9 lines, all in lib/design/brand.dart (lines 25, 27-30, 33-36); the pattern has no \b, unlike rawColor, yet matches the same lines.
git switch --detach <tag> checks out the commit a tag points to without creating a branch.
Choosing which brand a build or a shop gets is a product and deployment decision outside the theme code; DonHang.App ships one brand.
gallery_main.dart also builds its themes with buildTheme(donHangBrand, ...), for light and dark.
main.dart sets no themeMode, so MaterialApp uses its default ThemeMode.system and picks darkTheme when the platform brightness is dark, theme otherwise.
claims.source_hint: Flutter API: MaterialApp.themeMode, MaterialApp.darkTheme; examples/don-hang @ stage-3: DonHang.App/lib/main.dart:36-44

claims.text: grep -r searches every file under the given directory, -n prefixes each printed line with its line number, -E reads the pattern as an extended regular expression in which | means alternation.
